access.heading: Users and access
access.lede: Everyone this deployment knows, and the bank connections each of them may touch. Identity comes from the identity provider; access is granted here. A viewer may see a connection's orders, statements and schedules; an operator may also submit a payment at it.
access.lede_no_user_list: A subject appears below once it has signed in or once it holds a grant, so there is no user list to maintain here. Administrators come from the identity provider's claim and hold no grant.
access.lede_oversight: Oversight is the one grant that names no connection. It gives read-only access to every connection and to the audit rows that belong to none: sign-ins, service starts and grants themselves. It changes nothing anywhere, including on this page.
access.name: Name
access.no_connections: No connections are registered, so there is nothing to grant.
access.nobody: Nobody has signed in yet and nothing has been granted.
access.other_way_round: Read the same grants the other way round: who can reach one bank.
access.oversight_why: These accounts read every bank connection and the whole audit trail. They cannot submit a payment, register a connection, manage a webhook or a schedule, or grant access to anybody, themselves included.
access.subject: Subject
access.title: Access
access.ungranted_why: These accounts can sign in, and their console stays empty until somebody grants them a connection. Administrators appear here too: the role is a claim in their token from the identity provider, and it already reaches every connection without a grant.
accounts.delete_keeps_grants: Deleting an account removes the login and keeps the grants. Revoke those on the Access page.
accounts.heading: Accounts
accounts.lede: Who may sign in to this deployment. An account is a login and nothing more. What someone may reach is granted on the Access page, one bank connection at a time.
accounts.lockouts_why: Failed sign-ins are counted per account name and per source address. Clear one to let somebody back in now.
accounts.none: No account has been created yet.
accounts.other_mode: This deployment authenticates against an identity provider, so these accounts sign nobody in. Prepare them here before you switch, or remove them after.
accounts.password_hint: At least 12 characters. It is stored hashed and cannot be read back, here or anywhere else.
accounts.provider_owns_these: Accounts are managed in your identity provider
accounts.provider_owns_these_body: This deployment authenticates against a provider, so an account made here would be stored and then refused at sign-in: a password is only accepted when there is no provider. Existing accounts stay listed above so they can be removed. To prepare for moving off the provider, run python -m painfree create-admin, which works in every mode.
accounts.subject_hint: The name this person signs in with. Grants are made to this name, so keep it stable.
accounts.title: Accounts
alerts.connections_uninitialised.why: Registered, and not yet able to submit anything. Open the key lifecycle and finish it; the last step is comparing the bank's keys against the bank's letter.
alerts.heading: Needs attention
alerts.key_jobs_unfinished.why_many: The worker has been asked for a key operation and has not answered yet.
alerts.key_jobs_unfinished.why_one: The worker has been asked for {action} on {connection}.
alerts.none: Nothing is parked, failing or waiting on a person. This counts only the connections you hold.
alerts.orders_failed.why: This service could not get the file to the bank. Open the order and replay it: the same file goes out again under the same MsgId.
alerts.schedules_failing.why: The bank was not reached. The window has not moved, so the next run asks for the missed days again.
alerts.webhooks_parked.why: Receiving nothing. The events each one missed are kept until it is resumed.
api.a_role_not_a_scope: a role, not a scope: no grant can carry it
api.admin_only: No grant carries this, neither a level nor oversight. Only an administrator holds it.
api.any_credential_none: None. Every documented endpoint demands a scope.
api.any_credential_why: These documented endpoints demand no scope. Every authenticated caller reaches them, whatever they were granted.
api.auth_me_tail: , which is the endpoint to call when a client wants to check what it holds before acting. If a request came back 403, compare the scopes above with the endpoint's row in the table below.
api.basic_credential: An account name and password from this deployment, sent as HTTP Basic.
api.basic_get_one: Ask an administrator of this deployment for an account, then send it on every request:
api.basic_lockout_value: Counted per account name and per source address, over a rolling window.
api.basic_mode: Basic mode: identity comes from an account in this deployment's own database, with the password hashed.
api.basic_sign_out: The console signs in through a form and carries a session cookie, so signing out of it works. A program holding a Basic credential keeps it until you change the password.
api.basic_throttle: Failed sign-ins are counted per account name and per source address, and lock after a threshold. An administrator clears a lockout on the Accounts page.
api.basic_tls: Basic sends the password on every request. Put this service behind a proxy that terminates TLS. A production process refuses to start until the deployment declares one.
api.basic_why: No identity provider is configured, so this service issues the credentials itself. An administrator creates them on the Accounts page.
api.development_mode: Development mode: identity comes from a request header and no token is verified. A production process refuses to start like this.
api.endpoints: Endpoints, and what each one needs
api.endpoints_lede: Read off the running router: every route's declared dependency is inspected, so an endpoint added without a privilege appears here without one.
api.english_notice: Endpoint paths, scope names, error codes, privilege descriptions and endpoint summaries are the API's own contract. They stay in English in every language this console offers, because a client matches on them literally.
api.get_a_token: Get a token from the provider and send it. A service uses a client-credentials grant; a person signs in as usual.
api.heading: API and access
api.lede: Everything this console does by hand, a program can do over HTTP. This page carries the schema, how a machine authenticates, and the privilege each endpoint needs, all read off this running service.
api.no_credential: no credential: an orchestrator probe, or the login flow itself
api.no_grants: none yet. Your login works; the console stays empty until an administrator grants you a bank connection.
api.no_roles_in_token: The token carried no roles at all. This deployment reads the id_token, and looked for the claim:
api.no_tokens: A JWT bearer token from the configured OIDC provider. There is no other way in, and painfree issues no tokens of its own.
api.no_tokens_why: There is no "create an API key" button here or anywhere else. Revoke a machine's access at the provider, in the same place you revoke a person's.
api.on_this_connection: on the connection this path names
api.oversight_derived: That is every scope this service names :read, and no other. The set is derived from the scope names, so no privilege that changes something can enter it.
api.privileges_lede: Two roles and two grant levels. A role comes from your identity provider's claim; a level comes from a grant an administrator made, and applies to one connection. The oversight column is the one grant that names no connection: read-only, everywhere. ✓ marks a scope you hold somewhere. The table is generated from painfree.identity, the module the server authorises with.
api.public_paths: Reachable with no credential at all: the two orchestrator probes and the login endpoints. Nothing else. The middleware refuses an unauthenticated request before any route is reached.
api.role_admin: Everything, on every connection, including granting access.
api.role_member: What you may touch is per connection, and is granted here rather than claimed in your token. See below.
api.roles_note: Roles are what the provider granted; the scope claim can only narrow that, never widen it. A token carrying scope: payments:submit and no role grants nothing at all.
api.schema_note: These three need a credential like everything else. A browser that is signed in here is already carrying one; a program fetching openapi.json sends the same bearer token it would send to any other endpoint.
api.scopes_none: none, which is why you are being refused
api.scopes_oversight: The read scopes are held on every connection and on the audit rows that name none. Any scope here that is not one of those comes from a grant on the connections listed above, and is held on those only.
api.scopes_per_connection: Held on the connections listed above and on no others. A route that names a different connection is refused whatever this row says.
api.unmapped: The token also carried role names this deployment does not map. They grant nothing and are not kept; the count is:
audit.empty: No audit event matches this filter. The trail is append-only: an empty result means nothing was recorded under these terms, not that something was removed.
audit.heading: Audit trail
audit.lede: Every action this service took, who asked for it, and how it went. Append-only: nothing here can be edited or removed, by this console or by anything else. Each row carries the correlation ids that tie it to a request in the log stream and to the thing it happened to.
audit.reading_a_row_ids: request_id is the same value the JSON log lines carry, so docker logs | grep <request_id> reconstructs the whole request this row came from. seq is the append order and never repeats; event_id is what to quote outside this database.
audit.reading_a_row_redaction: A field shown as "***" was redacted by painfree.logging.redact on the way in, and the unredacted value was never stored. Redaction is by field name, so a harmless field that shares a name with a credential is hidden too.
audit.title: Audit
bank.note: Shown exactly as the bank sent it, in the bank's own language. This console does not translate what a bank says.
bank_keys.accept: These match the letter: accept the bank's keys
bank_keys.authentication_label: Authentication key (X002) as printed on the letter
bank_keys.confirm_body: Type the two values from the bank's letter. Nothing is filled in for you. Spaces and case are ignored; every one of the 64 hex characters has to match, and a prefix is not enough.
bank_keys.convention: Fingerprints computed with the convention this connection's letter uses:
bank_keys.decline_body: If the values do not match, or you have no letter to check them against, decline. The connection stays exactly as unusable as it is now, the keys are kept as evidence, and the refusal is written to the audit log with your name on it.
bank_keys.encryption_label: Encryption key (E002) as printed on the letter
bank_keys.grouped: Grouped in pairs, the way a letter prints them.
bank_keys.heading: Check the bank's keys
bank_keys.needs_scope: Accepting or declining the bank's keys needs the connections:write privilege.
bank_keys.read_this: Read this before you type anything.
bank_keys.read_this_body: The EBICS key-management response has no signature. Nothing in this service can tell whether the keys below came from your bank or from whoever was between you and it. The only control that exists is you, holding the bank's letter, comparing it character by character with what is on this page. A substituted encryption key means every payment file this service uploads is readable by whoever substituted it.
bank_keys.title: The bank's keys
bank_keys.why_placeholder: the E002 value on the letter does not match
chrome.subtitle: operator console
connection.compare: Compare them against the bank's letter
connection.no_bank_keys: The bank's keys have not been accepted yet.
connection.no_keys: No keys yet. Generate them from the key lifecycle page.
connection.staged: The bank's keys are waiting to be checked.
connection.staged_why: They arrived over HPB, which carries no signature, so this connection cannot submit anything until you compare them against the bank's letter.
connection.updated: The connection was updated. The change is in the audit log.
connection_access.heading: Who can reach
connection_access.lede: Everyone granted this bank connection. An operator here can submit a payment at this bank; a viewer can see what was paid and cannot pay. Administrators are not listed: they reach every connection and hold no grant.
connection_access.nobody: Nobody but an administrator can reach this connection.
connection_access.subject_note: The subject is the identity provider's sub claim, verbatim. It does not have to have signed in yet.
connection_access.subject_placeholder: the sub claim from the identity provider
connection_edit.digest_sent_body: INI or HIA has been sent, so the letter that was printed quotes the hash selected at the time. Changing this does not change any key the bank holds. It changes what a reprinted letter says, and the letter has to be printed, signed and posted again.
connection_edit.digest_sent_confirm: I will reprint and repost the letter
connection_edit.digest_sent_title: A letter for this connection has already gone to the bank
connection_edit.host_url_warning: The host URL is where signed order data is posted.
connection_edit.host_url_warning_body: A worker sends this connection's payments to whatever it says. The change is written to the audit log with the old value and the new one.
connection_edit.lede: HostID, PartnerID and UserID are not editable. They are what the bank knows this subscriber as, and the registered keys are bound to them. If one of them is wrong, register a second connection and initialise it.
connection_new.connection_id_hint: Lower-case, no spaces. It appears in every log line, audit row and URL for this bank.
connection_new.digest_certificate: certificate digest: sha256 over the certificate DER
connection_new.heading: Register a bank connection
connection_new.host_url_hint: Where EBICS requests are posted. Changing it later is audited.
connection_new.lede: The three identifiers are assigned by the bank and cannot be changed afterwards; the keys you register later are bound to them. This form sends nothing to the bank. It creates the connection, and the key lifecycle page then walks through INI, HIA and HPB.
connection_new.letter_digest: Which fingerprint does this bank's letter quote?
connection_new.letter_digest_hint: EBICS 3.0 carries keys inside certificates, and the two conventions give different values for the same key. Take this from the bank's letter rather than guessing; the wrong one makes a correct key look wrong.
connection_new.partner_id_hint: Your customer number with this bank.
connection_new.title: Register a connection
connection_new.user_id_hint: The subscriber this service signs as.
connections.empty_member: You have not been granted access to any bank connection.
connections.empty_member_link: API page shows what your account currently holds
connections.empty_member_where: Until then the rest of this console is empty for you too. The
connections.empty_member_why: Signing in gets you an account. Seeing a bank connection needs an administrator of this deployment to grant you one, at the level you need: viewer to see what was paid, operator to submit payments as well.
connections.heading: Bank connections
connections.lede: One row per EBICS subscriber: a HostID, PartnerID and UserID at one host URL. The key state runs from created through the INI, HIA and HPB exchanges to ready, and only a connection that reads ready can accept payments. Open a row for its key lifecycle, its recent orders and who has access to it.
connections.lede_member: You are shown the connections you have been granted. There may be others in this deployment.
connections.lede_oversight: You hold deployment-wide oversight: every connection is listed, read-only. Nothing on these pages will let you change one.
connections.title: Connections
jobs.empty: No key operations have been requested for this connection.
key_state.bank_keys_received: the bank's keys arrived and nobody has checked them
key_state.keys_sent: both registrations sent, the bank's keys not fetched
keys.custody_body: The private halves are sealed with PAINFREE_KEY_ENCRYPTION_SECRET, a value that lives in one file on the host, deploy/secrets/custody_secret, and that no database backup contains. Lose it and nobody can read these keys again: this connection needs new keys, a new INI letter signed on paper and posted to the bank, and days before it can move money.
keys.custody_title: Back up the custody secret before you generate
keys.heading: Key lifecycle
keys.lede: The steps that initialise this connection, in order, and what each one has already done. Clicking a step queues a request for the worker process, which is the only place a private key is opened, and the result appears under the key operations below.
keys.reason_hint: Stored on the audit row. Say what happened.
keys.reason_placeholder: laptop with the export was lost
keys.renewal_body: Renewal mints a new generation and supersedes the old key. It does not tell the bank: register the replacement with another INI or HIA. Suspension takes a key out of service and keeps it on file, so the record of what was registered survives.
keys.staged: The bank's keys are waiting for your comparison.
keys.staged_why: The HPB response carries no signature, so nothing here can tell whether these keys are the bank's. Open the comparison and check them against the bank's letter; until then this connection cannot submit anything.
keys.step1_body: A006 to sign order data, X002 to authenticate requests, E002 for the bank to encrypt to. The private halves are sealed by the worker and are never readable from this process.
keys.step2_body: Registers the signature key. The request carries no signature of its own, because the key it delivers is what a signature would be checked against. The bank refuses a second INI, so it is sent once.
keys.step3_body: Registers the authentication and encryption keys, the same way and for the same reason.
keys.step4: Print the INI letter, sign it, post it
keys.step4_body: The bank compares the fingerprints on the paper against the keys INI and HIA delivered. Nothing moves until the letter has arrived and the bank has processed it.
keys.step5_body: The bank sends its X002 and E002 keys, encrypted to ours. They are stored as pending and nothing uses them.
keys.step6: Compare the bank's keys against the bank's letter
keys.step6_body: The HPB response carries no signature, so this comparison is the whole trust decision. A connection whose bank keys have not been compared cannot submit a payment.
keys.title: Keys
lang.label: Language
lang.note: This changes what this console says, and nothing else. Amounts, dates and references in the files sent to the bank are unaffected.
letter.convention_certificate: SHA-256 over the X.509 certificate, in DER form
letter.convention_public_key: SHA-256 over the public key: the exponent and the modulus in hex, separated by a space
letter.declaration: I confirm that the hashes above are those of the keys registered for the subscriber named above.
letter.heading: EBICS initialisation letter
letter.hint: Print this page, sign it, and post it to the bank. The bank compares these hashes against the keys INI and HIA delivered.
letter.title: INI letter
nav.label: Console sections
order.attempts_hint: Read the BTF and the PmtTpInf of one attempt together to see what the bank was told about that message.
order.no_pain002: No pain.002 has named this order’s MsgId yet.
order.not_shown: The generated pain.001 is not shown here. Payments are reported by reference: the MsgId and the counts above identify this one.
order.reports_not_shown: The reports themselves are not shown; what they said about this order is summarised above. What every status code means is on the
order.requeued_why: The same order, the same stored pain.001 and the same MsgId go back to the worker. No second payment was created; if the bank already has this file it deduplicates on the MsgId.
orders.heading: Orders
orders.lede: What was submitted, where it got to, and what the bank said. accepted is queued here; submitted means the bank took the file, not that the payments were executed; acknowledged means a pain.002 has answered it; rejected is the bank refusing; failed is this service having given up. Open a failed order to replay it.
orders.title: Orders
payment_new.amount_hint: As you would write it, for example 1.00. The currency decides how many decimals are allowed.
payment_new.debtor_iban_hint: The account this connection is authorised to draw on. Spaces are ignored.
payment_new.end_to_end_id_hint: Your own identifier for this transfer, passed through unchanged. Left empty, the bank sees NOTPROVIDED.
payment_new.execution_date_hint: When the bank should execute it. A date in the past is usually executed on the next banking day.
payment_new.heading: Make a payment
payment_new.lede: One credit transfer, entered by hand. You will see the exact document this builds before anything is sent.
payment_new.not_initialised: This connection cannot send payments yet
payment_new.not_initialised_body: The bank has not activated this subscriber. Finish INI, HIA and HPB on the key lifecycle page first; a payment entered here would be refused.
payment_new.preview_hint: Nothing is sent by this button. It builds the document and shows it to you.
payment_new.reference_type_hint: Which reference this transfer carries. Not every type is allowed with every account, and the rule about the pair is checked when you preview.
payment_new.refused: This was not accepted, and nothing was sent
payment_new.remittance_hint: Unstructured text. Cannot be combined with a structured reference.
payment_new.scheme_hint: Leave at the default unless you are testing instant payments specifically.
payment_new.title: New payment
payment_preview.confirm: Send this payment to the bank
payment_preview.confirm_body: The document above is signed and uploaded to the bank. If the bank accepts it, money moves. There is no undo in this console: a payment already delivered is stopped by calling the bank.
payment_preview.document_hint: Exactly what will be signed and uploaded, except for the message id and the timestamp, which are minted when you confirm.
payment_preview.heading: This is what would be sent
payment_preview.lede: Built by the same code that submits. Read it, then confirm below to send it for real.
payment_preview.nothing_sent: Nothing has been sent, and nothing has been stored
payment_preview.nothing_sent_body: This document was built and checked against the official ISO 20022 schema. That is all it proves: no key has been opened, nothing has been signed, and the bank has not been contacted. A clean preview is not a promise that the bank will accept it.
payment_preview.title: Preview
profile.granted_none: No bank connection has been granted yet.
profile.label: Your account
recovery.banner_body: Generating a connection's first keys is refused until somebody confirms a copy exists.
recovery.banner_title: The custody secret has not been backed up
recovery.confirm: I hold a copy of the custody secret
recovery.confirm_body: Confirm only once the archive is somewhere that is not this host. Nobody is asked to paste the secret here: a console that could check it would be a console that could read it.
recovery.heading: Recovery
recovery.host_shell: a host shell command, not one to run inside a container
recovery.lede: What to hold a copy of, and how to tell which copy is the right one.
recovery.no_keys_yet: No keys are sealed yet, which is the best moment to do this
recovery.not_acknowledged: Nobody has confirmed a copy exists
recovery.relative_to: relative to the directory holding compose.yaml, on the host
recovery.rotation_unfinished: More than one: a rotation did not finish
recovery.title: Recovery
recovery.what_body: Every stored EBICS private key is sealed under the custody secret. It lives in one file on the host, it is in no database backup, and no copy of it exists anywhere this service can reach. Lose it and each bank connection needs new keys, an INI letter signed on paper and posted, and days before it can move money again.
recovery.what_title: One file, and nothing recovers it
recovery.where_body: On the host running this deployment, in the directory that holds compose.yaml. Both entries below are relative to it, and the command is a host shell command.
recovery.where_boundary: Not inside a container. The process serving this page is refused the custody secret and would not start if it were handed one, which is why it can describe the file without being able to read it.
replay.bank_said_nothing: nothing; this service never got it there
replay.heading: Replay
replay.no_second_payment_why: No new message is built. The pain.001 was built once when the order was accepted and is stored, so the worker re-sends the same bytes under the same MsgId and the same order id. A bank that already holds this file deduplicates it on that MsgId.
replay.title: Replay
replay.warning: This re-sends a payment file to a bank.
schedule.btf_edit_hint: What the bank publishes for this document. A wrong ServiceName comes back as EBICS_INVALID_ORDER_PARAMS hours later rather than as an error here, so take every field from the bank's own EBICS documentation.
schedule.cadence_hint: How often this runs. Every bank has a fair-use limit; the shortest this service accepts is 30 seconds.
schedule.controls_hint: Running now makes the schedule due immediately. A download worker claims it on its next poll and the result appears in the run ledger below. The process serving this page downloads nothing itself: only the worker can decrypt with the connection's private key.
schedule.created: The schedule is registered. A download worker claims it at {when}. Use Run now below to check that this bank answers the BTF before you rely on it.
schedule.empty_is_normal: the bank had nothing for this window, which is a normal result
schedule.failing_why: The last run did not finish, so the window has not moved: the days it asked for are asked for again on the next run. Fix the cause, then run it now rather than waiting for the cadence.
schedule.first_day_hint: The high-water mark is rewound to the day before this, so the next run asks from here to today. If that run then fails, the mark stays rewound and the following run asks for the whole widened window.
schedule.heading: Download schedule
schedule.never_run: This schedule has never run. Use Run now to check that this bank answers its BTF.
schedule.not_acknowledged: not acknowledged; the bank will serve this again

schedule.outstanding_days.one: {count} day before today has not been answered for
schedule.outstanding_days.other: {count} days before today have not been answered for

schedule.paused_why: No worker will claim this schedule. Its window is kept exactly where it is, so resuming asks the bank for the days that were missed rather than skipping them.
schedule.queued_refetch: The window was rewound and the schedule is due now.
schedule.queued_why: A download worker claims it on its next poll and the result appears in the run ledger below.
schedule.refetch_body: Ask the bank again for every day from the date below to today. Use this when a run failed and the days it missed have since been passed over, or when a bank re-issues a statement.
schedule.refetch_safe_why: A statement is stored under the identity the document itself carries, so one the bank serves twice is counted as a duplicate rather than stored a second time.
schedule.remove_why: Deleting this schedule drops its run ledger: the record of which windows were asked for and what came back. The statements it fetched are kept. If the schedule is coming back, pause it instead.
schedule.undated: This schedule sends no DateRange. The bank serves whatever it has pending for this BTF, and the receipt is what stops it being served again. There is no window to be behind on and nothing to re-fetch: an unacknowledged download comes back by itself.
schedule.unfinished: Runs that did not move the window
schedule.unfinished_why: Each of these asked the bank for a window and did not get it. The days they cover are still outstanding.
schedule.window_days_hint: Leave empty to send no DateRange at all. A dated schedule can be re-fetched; an undated one relies on the receipt.
schedule.window_hint: The mark moves only when the bank answered for the window, either with data or by saying it had none. A failed run leaves it where it is, so a missed day is asked for again rather than skipped.
schedule_new.btf_body: Which ServiceName a bank publishes for statements is per-bank configuration: EOP, STM or something else. A wrong one is answered with EBICS_INVALID_ORDER_PARAMS hours later rather than with an error here, so take these values from the bank's own EBICS documentation. The combinations below are common in Switzerland and are a starting point, not a default.
schedule_new.btf_fields_hint: Every field the bank's order parameters take. Leave the optional ones empty if the bank does not publish them.
schedule_new.btf_heading: Take the BTF from the bank's documentation
schedule_new.cadence_hint: How often this runs. A download is a multi-exchange conversation with a bank and every bank has a fair-use limit, so the shortest cadence this service accepts is 30 seconds.
schedule_new.connection_hint: The bank this asks. A schedule belongs to one connection and its window is that connection's.
schedule_new.description_hint: What this schedule is, for whoever reads the list later.
schedule_new.heading: Add a download schedule
schedule_new.lede: This service asks the bank for one document type on a fixed cadence and normalises whatever comes back. Most runs find nothing, which is the ordinary result rather than a failure.
schedule_new.title: Add a schedule
schedule_new.window_days_hint: How far back the first run asks. After that, each run asks from the day after the last one the bank answered for. Leave this empty to send no DateRange at all; the bank then serves what it has pending, and the receipt is what stops it being served twice. Only a dated schedule has a window that can be re-fetched.
schedules.behind_why: These schedules have days the bank has not answered for. The next run asks for them again; if it does not get them, re-fetch the window from the schedule's own page.
schedules.empty: No schedule is registered, so nothing is being fetched from any bank. Payments still go out, but no statement comes back. Add a schedule to start fetching.
schedules.failing_why: The last run did not reach the bank, or the bank refused it. Nothing has been fetched since, and the window has not moved, so the missed days are asked for again on the next run.
schedules.heading: Download schedules
schedules.lede: What this service fetches from each bank, and how often. A schedule is empty when the bank had nothing for that window, which is the ordinary result; failing when the last run could not reach the bank; paused when no worker will claim it. Open one to run it now, re-fetch a window or change its cadence.
schedules.no_date_range: no date range; the bank serves what is pending
schedules.title: Schedules
scheme_reason.bank_refused_instant: The bank refused instant, so the reserve message went instead
scheme_reason.preflight.amount_above_ins: The amount is above the instant ceiling, so this went normal before anything was sent
scheme_reason.preflight.instant_not_conf: Instant is not configured here, so this went normal before anything was sent
schemes.btf_hint: Ask your bank for the triplet it publishes. A wrong one comes back as EBICS_INVALID_ORDER_PARAMS.
schemes.ceiling_hint: Leave it empty for no ceiling. A transfer above it goes normal before anything is sent, and is refused outright if the caller asked for instant.
schemes.heading: Payment schemes
schemes.instant_offered: This connection can send instant payments
schemes.instant_unavailable: Instant is not configured, so this connection sends every payment as normal.
schemes.lede: Set what this bank calls a normal and an instant credit transfer. Leave a field empty to send nothing in it.
schemes.refusal_codes: Return codes that mean instant was refused
schemes.refusal_codes_hint: Separate them with spaces. Only these codes let an instant_or_normal payment fall back; every other refusal ends the order.
sign_in.heading: Sign in
sign_in.lede: This deployment issues its own accounts. Enter the account name and password an administrator gave you.
sign_in.no_accounts: Nothing signs in until an administrator account is created. Run this on the host where the service is installed:
sign_in.refused: That account name and password were not accepted. Check both and try again.
sign_in.throttled: Repeated failures lock the account name and the address you are coming from. A lockout expires by itself, and an administrator can clear it sooner.
sign_in.title: Sign in
signed_out.browser: If you typed this password into a password box the browser itself put on the screen, the browser keeps it and sends it again. Close every window of this browser to make it forget.
signed_out.heading: You are signed out
signed_out.lede: Your session here is ended. Any other browser or program using this account is unaffected.
signed_out.shared_machine: On a shared computer, close the browser before you walk away. Clearing this site's cookies is not enough.
signed_out.title: Signed out
statement.no_order: no order on this connection was submitted under
statements.empty: No statements have been ingested yet. They arrive from the download schedules.
statements.heading: Statements
statements.lede: Every statement the download schedules have ingested, normalised to JSON: which account it covers, its closing balance, how many entries it carries and, where one is known, the order it reports on. Open a statement to read its entries and the normalised document.
statements.title: Statements
status_code.ACCC: settled and credited to the beneficiary
status_code.ACCP: the file passed the customer-profile checks
status_code.ACFC: accepted, and the debtor's cover was checked
status_code.ACTC: the file passed the bank's technical checks
status_code.ACWC: accepted, with something the bank changed
status_code.ACWP: accepted, not yet posted to the creditor's account
status_code.BLCK: blocked at the bank; somebody there has to act
status_code.CANC: cancelled; it will not be executed
status_code.PART: some of the batch was accepted and some refused
status_code.PDNG: pending; the bank is still working on it
status_code.RJCT: refused; it will not be executed
status_codes.heading: Payment status codes
status_codes.lede: What a bank's pain.002 can say, and what this service does with each one. The table is rendered from the same mapping the reconciler decides with.
status_codes.levels: A status report carries a status at up to three levels: the whole message, one payment block, one transaction. The group status decides the order; the levels below it refine it, because a bank that partially accepts a file routinely lists only the transactions it refused. When the bank sends no group status, the levels below decide only if they all agree.
status_codes.not_ebics_body: A six-digit 091116 is about the transfer; a four-letter ACSP is about the payment. They live in different columns and are shown separately on every order.
status_codes.not_ebics_heading: These are not EBICS return codes.
status_codes.part_body: Part of the batch went through. Calling it rejected would make it replayable, and replaying a partly-executed batch re-sends the transactions the bank already accepted. The refused transactions are counted on the order page and carry the bank’s own reason code and text.
status_codes.part_heading: PART is an acknowledgement, not a rejection.
status_codes.terminal: An order is moved out of accepted or submitted and nothing else. A report about an order that is already terminal, or that a worker currently holds, is recorded against the order and changes no state.
status_codes.title: Payment status codes
status_codes.unknown: A code that is not in this table moves nothing. It is logged by name and written to the audit trail, and the order stays in the state it was in.
subject.granted_oversight: Granted deployment-wide oversight. It began on their next request.
subject.heading: Access for
subject.holds_nothing_tail: They can sign in; their console is empty until a connection is granted below.
subject.holds_oversight: This subject reads every bank connection and the whole audit trail, including the rows that name no connection: sign-ins, service starts and grants. Granted by
subject.lede: The bank connections this subject may touch, and at what level. This is the whole of what they hold: everything else in the console is refused to them.
subject.oversight_offer: Read-only review of the whole deployment: every connection's orders, statements, schedules and webhook endpoints, and every audit row. It changes nothing, not a payment, not a connection, not a webhook or a schedule, and not this page. A holder cannot grant access to anybody, themselves included.
subject.regrant_note: Granting a connection this subject already holds changes the level rather than adding a second grant.
subject.revoked_oversight: Revoked deployment-wide oversight. It stopped working on their next request; no sign-out and no restart is needed.
subject.revoked_when: It stopped working on their next request; no sign-out and no restart is needed.
webhook.controls_hint: A test event proves that the endpoint answers and that its signature verifies, before a real payment depends on it. Pausing keeps every event queued for later; parking is the same state, entered by this service after repeated failures rather than by you.
webhook.heading: Webhook endpoint
webhook.no_deliveries: Nothing has been owed to this endpoint yet. Send a test event to find out whether it works before a payment depends on it.
webhook.parked: Parked: this endpoint is receiving nothing

webhook.parked_owed.one: {count} event is being kept for it. Fix the endpoint, then resume: everything it missed is delivered, oldest first.
webhook.parked_owed.other: {count} events are being kept for it. Fix the endpoint, then resume: everything it missed is delivered, oldest first.

webhook.parked_why: {failures} deliveries in a row exhausted their retries, so delivery was stopped rather than left to grow.
webhook.paused_why: Nothing is delivered and no new event is queued for this endpoint while it is paused.
webhook.pinged: A test event was queued as
webhook.pinged_why: It goes out the way a real event does, signed and retried and recorded, so watch for it in the deliveries below. It sits behind anything this endpoint is already owed.

webhook.remove_why.one: Deleting this endpoint also drops the {count} event still owed to it. It is not re-created. If the endpoint is coming back, pause it instead.
webhook.remove_why.other: Deleting this endpoint also drops the {count} events still owed to it. They are not re-created. If the endpoint is coming back, pause it instead.

webhook.rotating: A secret rotation is in flight
webhook.rotating_why: Since {since} every delivery is signed with both the new secret (generation {generation}) and the one it replaced, so an endpoint that has not been reconfigured yet still verifies what it receives. Finish the rotation once your receiver holds the new value.
webhook.sealed: sealed, and not readable by this service
webhook.url_hint: Events already queued go to the new address; the URL is read at delivery time, not when the event was created.
webhook_new.connection_hint: Leave this at every connection unless the endpoint should only hear about one bank.
webhook_new.description_hint: What this endpoint is, for whoever reads the list later.
webhook_new.event_types_hint: At least one. A type not ticked is never sent, and adding one later does not resend what was missed.
webhook_new.heading: Register a webhook endpoint
webhook_new.lede: This service POSTs a signed JSON event to this URL every time one of the chosen things happens. The signing secret is generated here and shown on the next screen once; it cannot be shown again.
webhook_new.title: Register a webhook
webhook_new.url_hint: An http or https URL that answers 2xx within 15 seconds. A redirect is not followed.
webhook_secret.already_registered_tail: the first time. Nothing was created a second time, and the secret from that first registration is not shown again.
webhook_secret.already_registered_why: The registration was submitted twice, by a reload or a retry, and the same idempotency key registered
webhook_secret.copy_now: Copy this now. It is not shown again.
webhook_secret.copy_now_why: It is stored sealed, and no screen, API call or support request can produce it a second time. If it is lost, rotate the endpoint's secret and configure the new value.
webhook_secret.old_still_signing: The old secret is still signing
webhook_secret.old_still_signing_why: Every delivery now carries a signature under both secrets, and your receiver accepts if either verifies, so nothing is refused while you switch it over. Once it is using the new value, come back and finish the rotation, which stops the old one signing.
webhook_secret.rotate_instead: If you did not keep it, rotate the endpoint's secret below.
webhook_secret.title: Signing secret
webhook_secret.verifying_body: Each request carries X-Painfree-Timestamp and X-Painfree-Signature. The signature is one or more comma-separated v1=<hex> entries, more than one only while a secret is being rotated. Accept the request if any of them verifies:
webhook_secret.verifying_tail: Compute it over the raw bytes you received, never over a re-serialisation of your own parse; compare in constant time; then refuse anything whose timestamp is older than your replay window. The timestamp is inside the MAC and cannot be re-dated.
webhooks.empty: No endpoint is registered, so nothing receives this service's events. Payments still go to the bank, but nobody is told what happened to them. Register an endpoint to start receiving them.
webhooks.heading: Webhooks
webhooks.lede: Where this service pushes its events, and whether each endpoint is keeping up. One that stops answering is retried and then parked: nothing more is sent to it, and the events it missed are kept until somebody resumes it. Paused is the same state, entered by hand.
webhooks.parked_why: Receiving nothing. The events each one missed are still queued and are delivered when it is resumed.
webhooks.title: Webhooks
